क्या चार हजार करोड़ का दांव बॉक्स ऑफिस पर फेल हो गया? 

फिल्म Ramayana का बजट 4000 करोड़ है और प्रोड्यूसर नामित मल्होत्रा इसे लेकर बिल्कुल भी परेशान नहीं हैं। 

उनका कहना है कि अगर फिल्म से पैसे नहीं बने तो वे मर्चेंडाइज और थीम पार्क से कमाई करेंगे। 

नामित का दावा है कि Ramayana सिर्फ दो फिल्में नहीं बल्कि एक पूरी फिलॉसफी है जिसे वे आगे बढ़ाएंगे। 

प्लान में वीडियो गेम, टॉयज, गैजेट्स, टीवी शो, एनिमेटेड प्रोजेक्ट्स और ब्रॉडवे म्यूजिकल शामिल हैं। 

फिल्म का दूसरा पार्ट 2028 में आएगा और मेकर्स इसे एक बड़े यूनिवर्स के रूप में देख रहे हैं। 

क्या आपको लगता है कि बॉलीवुड के लिए सिर्फ टिकट सेल्स के बिना इतनी बड़ी इन्वेस्टमेंट निकालना मुमकिन है? 🤔🎬🔥

ctx.title: Ramayana producer Namit Malhotra not worried about recovering Rs-4000-crore budget through box office; plans to make money through merch, theme parks
ctx.summary: The producer is looking beyond ticket sales for his ambitious two-part adaptation and believes there are several ways to make the massive investment work.
ctx.text:
Ramayana , or as it is internationally titled Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, released in theatres on November 5 ahead of Diwali 2026. Starring Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana, the film opened on a decent note but picked up momentum as the first weekend concluded. With the two-part epic, mounted on a whopping ₹ 4000 crore budget, one would think that producer Namit Malhotra would be stressed about how the movie will fare at the box office. However, that does not seem to be the case. The producer is looking beyond ticket sales for his ambitious two-part adaptation and believes there are several ways to make the massive investment work.
While the scale of the movie is massive, Namit is confident that the Ramayana has enough potential to find an audience across different formats. In an interview with CNN, the producer said, “I'm not motivated by the bean-counter logic of, ‘How much money did we make or not make'. If we don’t make money with the movies, we’ll make it in the merchandise. If we don’t make it in the merchandise, we’ll make it in the theme park. If we don’t make it in the theme park, we’ll make it some other way.”
During an earlier conversation with the same publication, he spoke about the film with the conviction of someone who believes the story itself gives the project a strong foundation. "I don’t want to sound spiritual as a businessman," he said. “But honestly … you can’t do this right and not succeed. To me, there’s one fundamental truth: that if we do ‘Ramayana’ well, and if people like it, financially we’ll be fine. That's my fundamental belief. There’s no way to argue it. There’s no way to debate it. And I don’t think anybody in the world is smart enough to counter it with scientific or commercial logic.”
It is not the first time he has spoken about the adaptation and that he has several plans for the epic. At the film's Telugu pre-release event in Hyderabad, he explained that the larger ambition was always to create something that could continue engaging audiences long after the two films have been released.
He had said, “The word Ramayana, as we all know, is really a philosophy. It is a word that we have grown up with. All of us have, from our fathers, our grandfathers, our multi-generations have known the story of an epic called the Ramayana. When we were conceiving this, this was not meant to be just a film. This was meant to be much more than that.”
He added that the intention is not to bring the story to a close after two films but to use them as a starting point for exploring the larger world of the epic: “The idea is not to make one or two movies and stop the journey of Rama. In fact, it is to start this journey. On the back of this movie, we can actually start to open up the different areas of engagement.”
At the same event, the producer had also presented a behind-the-scenes video that offered a glimpse into the proposed expansion of the Ramayana universe. The plans include video games based on the epic, along with merchandise spanning apparel, toys, gadgets and home furnishings.
The team is also looking at developing spin-off stories through origin films, television shows and animated projects. The plans include theme park experiences and a Broadway musical adaptation. Virtual reality, augmented reality and metaverse experiences are also part of the larger vision.
The two-part epic, which is directed by Nitesh Tiwari , also stars Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, Addinath Kothare as Bharat, Rakul Preet Singh as Surpankha, Vivek Oberoi as Vidyutjihva, Arun Govil as Dashrath, Indira Krishnan as Kaushalya, Lara Dutta as Kaikeyi among others. The film is closing in on ₹ 400 crore net at the box office net. The second part is scheduled for 2028 release.
Monica Yadav is a senior entertainment journalist with Hindustan Times Entertainment, based in Mumbai, with nearly 11 years of experience covering Bollywood, Hollywood and Asian entertainment, including Korean, Chinese and Thai cin
